title: tc-approval-card
description: An agent's request for approval, with Approve / Deny, an optional countdown, and a compact row once decided.

heading.description: The action, e.g. "Send campaign email" – the group's name

risk.description: Tinted badge in the header; leave out to hide it

details.description: Key-value rows in the preview, e.g. To, Subject, Scheduled

errorLabel.description: Shown under the buttons when an onApprove promise rejects

expiresIn.description: Seconds until the request expires and is denied with reason "timeout"

allowStopTimer.description: Show a "Stop" button next to the countdown that turns the time limit off (WCAG 2.2.1). Default true

stopTimerLabel.description: Its label – the countdown ("Expires in 42 seconds…") describes it

allowAlways.description: Show the "Always allow this action" checkbox. Default true

shortcuts.description: Show ⌘↵ / Esc hints on the buttons (the shortcuts work either way). Default true

actions.description: Where the buttons sit: on the gray tray below the card or inside the white card. Default: "tray" in the Standard look, "card" in the Clean look

why.description: "Why you're seeing this": one line on what made the agent ask, e.g. the rule or threshold it met

consequences.description: What happens if the person approves, and if they deny – one sentence each

ifApproveLabel.description: The heading of the approve consequence

ifDenyLabel.description: The heading of the deny consequence

editableDetails.description: Shows "Edit arguments", which turns the text details into fields; each change fires tc-details-change

evidence.description: Sources the request rests on, shown as chips

evidenceLabel.description: The heading of the evidence chips

editable.description: With `editableDetails`: false keeps this row read-only. Element values are always read-only

ApprovalDetail.description: A key-value row of the preview: the value is text or an element (cloned)

detail.description: A quiet second part, e.g. "p. 4" or "2 h ago"

ApprovalEvidence.description: A source the request rests on, shown as a chip: a link with `href`, else a button that fires tc-evidence-select
